source: Cue categories adapted from NIST (2021) phishing guidance.

lessons.title: Check who really sent it
lessons.summary: Display names are easy to fake. What matters is the domain after the @ sign.
look_for: Swapped characters, such as l for i or 0 for o
Extra words or hyphens, such as northbridge-admin
A Reply-To address that differs from the sender
lessons.safe_action: Compare the full domain with one you know is genuine.

lessons.title: Look before you click
lessons.summary: Link text can say anything. Check the real destination and read its domain from right to left.
look_for: Link text that differs from the real destination
Brand names used as a label in front of another domain
http:// rather than https:// on a sign-in page
lessons.safe_action: Open important sites from a bookmark or by typing the address.

lessons.title: Slow down when you are rushed
lessons.summary: Attackers create panic so you act before you think. Genuine organizations give reasonable notice.
look_for: Threats of cancellation, deletion, or fines
Shouting words such as FINAL NOTICE or URGENT
lessons.example: Your enrollment will be cancelled at 5:00 PM today
lessons.safe_action: Pause, then verify through a channel you already trust.

lessons.title: Question surprise files
lessons.summary: Attachments you did not expect are one of the most common ways to deliver malware.
look_for: Invoices or labels from companies you do not use
Pressure to open the file quickly
lessons.example: Invoice_88213.zip from a bank you have never used
lessons.safe_action: Open only expected files; when unsure, ask the sender another way.

lessons.title: Never share secrets
lessons.summary: No genuine organization asks for your password or one-time code by email, chat, or phone.
look_for: Requests to reply with a username and password
Requests to forward a verification code
Sign-in pages reached from a message or pop-up
lessons.example: Reply with the 6-digit code we sent to your phone
lessons.safe_action: Keep passwords and codes private and turn on multi-factor authentication.

lessons.title: Verify the address bar
lessons.summary: A copied logo and a padlock do not make a site genuine. The padlock means the connection is encrypted, not that the owner is trustworthy.
look_for: Domains that add words or hyphens
Unexpected requests to sign in again
Arriving from a link instead of a bookmark
lessons.safe_action: Use bookmarks for important sites and check the domain every time.
